result: ALL transplantation into mice causes rapid expansion of leukemic cells and selective suppression of lymphopoiesis and erythropoiesis, with modest effects on myeloid cell production.
evaluation: Claims C3 and C42-C47 collectively demonstrate that ALL cells expand rapidly in bone marrow while causing >10-fold reductions in B cell progenitors and erythrocytes by 2-3 weeks, with only modest (2-fold) reductions in neutrophils. The data from Figure 1 provide clear temporal kinetics supporting lineage-specific suppression.

result: ALL cells express elevated lymphotoxin α1β2 which activates LTβR signaling in MSCs to downregulate IL7 production and suppress lymphopoiesis.
evaluation: Claims C4-C7 and C53-C60 demonstrate that ALL cells express higher LTα/LTβ than normal B cells (Figures 2A-B), that overexpression of LTα/LTβ enhances IL7 suppression and lethality (Figure 2—supplement 1B-E), and that LTβR-Ig treatment restores lymphopoiesis and reduces ALL growth (Figures 2C-I). The mechanistic link is well-supported by multiple complementary approaches.

result: Genetic or pharmacological disruption of LTβR signaling in MSCs selectively restores lymphopoiesis but not erythropoiesis or myelopoiesis, reduces leukemic growth, and extends survival.
evaluation: Claims C10-C13 and C76-C80 demonstrate that both LTβR-Ig treatment and genetic deletion of LTβR in MSCs (LTβRΔ mice) restore lymphopoiesis (Figures 2D, 4C-E) but not erythropoiesis or myelopoiesis (Figures 2E-G, 4G-J), reduce ALL numbers (Figures 2H, 4F, 4K), and extend survival by ~1 week (Figures 2I, 4L). The lineage-specific effect is consistently demonstrated.

result: Ltb-deficient ALL cells cannot induce IL7 downregulation or suppress lymphopoiesis, proliferate less, and extend mouse survival.
evaluation: Claims C81-C84 demonstrate that genetic deletion of Ltb in ALL cells prevents IL7 downregulation (Figure 4N), maintains normal lymphopoiesis (Figure 4O), reduces ALL proliferation (Figure 4P), and extends survival (Figure 4Q). Even 3-fold higher numbers of Ltb-/- ALLs fail to suppress IL7 (Figures 4R-S), confirming the requirement for lymphotoxin expression by leukemic cells.

result: ALL induces major transcriptional changes in MSCs including inflammatory gene signatures and downregulation of multiple hematopoietic cytokines, but only IL7 downregulation is LTβR-dependent.
evaluation: Claims C61-C71 demonstrate through RNA-seq that ALL induces 322 DEGs in MSCs with strong inflammatory signatures (Figure 3A-C), downregulates KITL, IL7, IGF1, and CSF1 (Figure 3D), but only IL7 downregulation is reversed by LTβR-Ig treatment (Figure 3D). The specificity of LTβR signaling for IL7 regulation is clearly established.

result: The DNA damage response pathway promotes lymphotoxin α1β2 expression through NFκB activation in pre-leukemic and leukemic cells.
evaluation: Claims C8 and C89-C95 demonstrate that Artemis-deficient pre-B cells (which accumulate DNA damage) express elevated LTα/LTβ (Figure 5—supplement 1A), induce LTβR-dependent IL7 downregulation (Figure 5—supplement 1B), and that Etoposide treatment induces dose-dependent LTα upregulation (Figure 5—supplement 1F-G) that is blocked by NFκB inhibitor IMD0354 (Figure 5—supplement 1H). The pathway is mechanistically defined.

result: CXCR4 signaling promotes lymphotoxin α1β2 expression in ALL cells in vitro and in vivo.
evaluation: Claims C9 and C98-C103 demonstrate that CXCL12 treatment induces LTα upregulation in vitro in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 5A), with synergistic effects when combined with Etoposide (Figure 5B), and that AMD3100 treatment reduces LTα expression in vivo (Figure 5C) while increasing CXCR4 surface expression (Figure 5D). The CXCR4-lymphotoxin axis is well-supported.

result: CXCR4 antagonist treatment prevents ALL-induced IL7 downregulation, maintains lymphopoiesis, reduces ALL growth, and extends survival.
evaluation: Claims C14-C15 and C105-C108 demonstrate that oral CXCR4 antagonist treatment maintains IL7 expression at normal levels (Figure 5F), preserves developing B cell numbers (Figure 5G), reduces ALL numbers in bone marrow and periphery (Figure 5H), and significantly extends survival (Figure 5I). The therapeutic potential of CXCR4 blockade is clearly demonstrated.

result: IL7/anti-IL7 antibody complex treatment increases lymphopoiesis and reduces ALL growth, demonstrating that lymphotoxin-mediated IL7 suppression accelerates leukemia progression.
evaluation: Claims C86-C88 demonstrate that IL7/aIL7 treatment significantly increases developing B cell numbers (Figure 4—supplement 1B) and reduces ALL numbers in bone marrow, spleen, and blood (Figure 4—supplement 1C). This gain-of-function experiment confirms that IL7 suppression causally contributes to ALL growth advantage.

result: AML cells also express LTβ, induce LTβR-dependent IL7 downregulation in MSCs, and LTβR-Ig treatment partially restores lymphopoiesis, reduces AML growth, and extends survival.
evaluation: Claims C116-C121 demonstrate that MLL-AF9+ AML cells express higher LTβ than normal myeloid cells (Figure 6A), induce IL7 downregulation that is blocked by LTβR-Ig (Figure 6B), and that LTβR-Ig treatment partially restores B lymphopoiesis (Figure 6C) but not erythropoiesis (Figure 6D), reduces AML growth, and extends survival (Figures 6E-F). The mechanism extends beyond ALL to AML.

result: LTB transcript abundance inversely correlates with relapse-free survival in pediatric B-ALL patients and overall survival in AML patients.
evaluation: Claims C52 and C113 demonstrate statistically significant inverse correlations between LTB expression and patient outcomes in both B-ALL (Figure 2—supplement 1A, p=0.000785) and AML (Figure 6—supplement 1A, p=0.0409) patient cohorts. The clinical relevance is established, though the correlations are observational.

result: ALL cells express higher CXCR4 levels than normal B cell progenitors and migrate more efficiently toward CXCL12 gradients, suggesting enhanced bone marrow retention.
evaluation: Claims C109-C111 demonstrate that ALLs express significantly higher CXCR4 than non-leukemic B cell progenitors in vivo (Figure 5J) and show enhanced chemotaxis toward CXCL12 in vitro (Figure 5K). The inference about enhanced retention (C111) is reasonable but not directly tested.

result: Blocking TNFα, IL1β, IFNα, or IFNγ does not prevent IL7 downregulation, rescue hematopoiesis, or reduce ALL growth.
evaluation: Claims C72-C74 demonstrate through negative control experiments that blocking other inflammatory cytokines (TNFα, IL1β, IFNα, IFNγ) does not replicate the effects of LTβR blockade (Figure 3—supplement 1A-I). These controls strengthen the specificity of the LTβR pathway but represent negative findings.

result: LTβR signaling in MSCs does not control CXCL12 expression under homeostatic conditions and does not affect ALL homing to bone marrow.
evaluation: Claim C75 demonstrates that ALL cells home equally to bone marrow in control and LTβRΔ mice (Figure 4A), consistent with prior work showing LTβR does not regulate CXCL12 at homeostasis. This control experiment rules out effects on homing but is a negative finding.

result: MLL-AF9 induction increases AML cell frequency and myeloid subsets while reducing erythroid and lymphoid subsets.
evaluation: Claims C114-C115 demonstrate that DOX-induced MLL-AF9 expression increases NGFR+ AML cells and myeloid populations (Figure 6—supplement 1B-C) while reducing erythroid and lymphoid cells (Figure 6—supplement 1D-E). This characterizes the AML model but is descriptive.

result: ALL cells induce small but significant CXCL12 downregulation in MSCs that is partly LTβR-dependent, but other cytokines (KITL, IGF1, CSF1) are downregulated independently of LTβR.
evaluation: Claims C132 and C136 demonstrate through RNA-seq that CXCL12 shows modest LTβR-dependent downregulation while KITL, IGF1, and CSF1 are downregulated independently of LTβR (Figure 3D). This establishes pathway specificity but the CXCL12 effect is small and the functional significance unclear.

result: IL7R signaling is not sufficient to upregulate lymphotoxin α1β2 expression in ALL cells despite promoting IL7Rα internalization.
evaluation: Claim C101 demonstrates through negative data that IL7 treatment does not induce LTα expression in ALL cells even at high concentrations (Figure 5—supplement 2A-B), contrasting with prior findings in lymphoid tissue inducer cells. This is a negative control finding.

result: Artemis deficiency does not impact myeloid-erythroid production.
evaluation: Claim C92 demonstrates that Artemis-deficient pre-B cells do not affect myeloid or erythroid lineages (Figure 5—supplement 1D-E), consistent with the lineage-specific effects of LTβR signaling. This is a negative control finding.

result: Background knowledge establishing that leukemias alter bone marrow microenvironment, that MSCs and ECs produce hematopoietic cytokines, and that CXCR4 and LTβR signaling regulate hematopoiesis.
evaluation: Claims C1-C2 and C17-C41 establish the scientific context through citations to prior literature. These are knowledge claims that frame the study but do not represent new findings. They are appropriately cited and provide necessary background.

result: Interpretive claims proposing that leukemias exploit physiological mechanisms for competitive advantage, that the LTβR-CXCR4 axis forms a feed-forward loop, and potential therapeutic implications.
evaluation: Claims C16 and C122-C140 represent interpretations and speculations about mechanisms and therapeutic potential. While these are reasonable inferences from the data, they involve speculation about feed-forward loops (C129), therapeutic applications (C135), and mechanistic explanations (C139-C140) that require additional validation. The interpretations are plausible but extend beyond what is directly demonstrated.
